analysis: What changed versus the 7:00 AM brief: the bounce strengthened into late morning but cooled off its highs — the S&P 500 is now +1.00% (vs +0.38% at the open) and the Nasdaq +1.73% (vs +1.28%), while the Dow recovered from -474 points at the open to roughly flat. Nvidia is the tell: +7.05% at the open, now +4.40% and off its $194.90 session high — early buyers are taking profits into the bounce. Apple flipped positive (+0.21%) after lagging at the open, and Microsoft is nearly flat, so the megacap split is narrowing rather than widening. The VIX compressed further to 23.88 from the 7 AM reading of 26.70, and the Michigan sentiment beat (51.0 vs 47.5 expected) with cooling one-year inflation expectations (4.3% vs 4.7%) gave the tape a second, softer tailwind after the hot payrolls print. Signal vs noise: the breadth of the late-morning bounce (six of 11 sectors higher, IT leading) and the VIX compression are signal; the Anthropic IPO repricing ($1.2-1.3T discussed vs $1.5T before the rout) is the liveest read on AI valuations and matters more than any single chip quote. The Walleye Capital de-risking and Nomura's warning that vol-control selling queues into Friday are the counterweight — the bounce is happening against forced selling, not just dip-buying. WSB is split between a bull-trap read (quant funds still need to cut, Iran weekend risk) and a V-shape read (QQQ higher 5 days after a >6% drop about 81% of the time). DraftKings (-28%) and Moderna's flip remain the earnings bookends: guidance cuts are still punished, raised outlooks are still paid.

headlines.headline: The bounce strengthened into late morning: at 10:21 a.m. ET the S&P 500 was up 1.00% at 7,426.29 and the Nasdaq Composite up 1.73% at 24,736.20, while the Dow recovered to roughly flat at 51,530.05 after opening down 474 points.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce broadened beyond the open and the Dow clawed back its whole early loss — but the gains are still concentrated in the names hit hardest Thursday, not a broad rally.

headlines.headline: Nvidia cooled from +7.05% at the open to +4.40% at $189.60 in late-morning trading (prior close $181.60), off its $194.90 session high; AMD and Micron were also off their early highs.
headlines.why_it_matters: Early buyers are taking profits into the bounce — the chip recovery is real but already fading from its best levels, so the open's momentum is not compounding.

headlines.headline: Megacaps mostly extended gains by late morning: Meta +3.07% to $623.66, Tesla +4.58% to $359.43, Alphabet +1.96% to $288.12 and Amazon +1.30% to $263.60, while Microsoft was nearly flat at -0.08% ($535.51) and Apple flipped positive to +0.21% ($344.89).
headlines.why_it_matters: The megacap split is narrowing — Apple flipped from laggard to green and Microsoft steadied — so the recovery is spreading beyond chips, though Microsoft still has not joined it.

headlines.headline: Preliminary November Michigan consumer sentiment rose to 51.0 from 48.0 in October, beating the 47.5 consensus; one-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3% from 4.7% and five-year expectations to 3.4% from 3.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A better-than-expected mood print plus cooling inflation expectations eases the stagflation worry — a softer second tailwind after the hot payrolls report, though the survey was taken before Tuesday's election results.

headlines.headline: Anthropic's planned IPO is being repriced: prospective investors are discussing a $1.2-1.3 trillion valuation, down from $1.4-1.5 trillion before the selloff and as high as $2 trillion in early October, and some doubt the roadshow planned for the week of Nov 9 can proceed on schedule; Anthropic declined to comment.
headlines.why_it_matters: The marquee AI IPO is now the liveest read on AI valuations — a delayed or discounted Anthropic listing would confirm the repricing driving the chip tape, not just reflect it.

headlines.headline: $17 billion hedge fund Walleye Capital told investors Thursday it will trim its internal equity long-short business, cut a substantial portion of its equity team and return a portion of capital after its worst month since March 2020; tech-focused equity long-short funds fell more than 4% on Thursday, wiping out year-to-date gains.
headlines.why_it_matters: Thursday's rout forced real de-risking at a big multi-strategy fund — Friday's bounce is happening against forced selling and layoffs, not just dip-buying, which is why the tape stays fragile.

usac.why_it_matters: USAC +2.52% to $24.85 in late-morning trading; no fresh company news. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
